decisions.title: ADR relevance scan
decisions.detail: docs/DESIGN/adr/ has 4 ADRs, all about the S3f2658/S862203 no-halt-agent ptyhost mechanism (thin-holder ptyhost, cgroup escape, pipe-mode offset replay). ADR-0001 (detached ptyhost for agent survival) and ADR-0002 (ptyhost is a thin holder — orchestration stays in palmux2) both list internal/tab/claudetui (now internal/tab/agenttui, renamed by S0e8afb) and cmd/palmux (ptyhost subcommand) as affected — this Sprint touches internal/tab/agenttui/{daemon,manager}.go to port the S339021-3 notify-hub agentKind/TabName stamping from the maultiagent reference branch, so both ADRs are in scope as a conformance constraint (not a violation to resolve): the port must only add data (TabName field passthrough, hook-dispatch calls) to the orchestration layer already living in palmux2/agenttui, and must NOT touch internal/ptyhost's protocol, ring, or socket framing. ADR-0003 (cgroup escape) and ADR-0004 (agent pipe-mode/offset-replay, which governs claudeagent specifically) are not touched — codex/opencode are TUI-only (agent.Capabilities modes=['tui'], no stream-json 'agent' mode), so claudeagent.Client / the pipe-mode ptyhost path is untouched by this Sprint.

decisions.title: Story validation and granularity — kept as originally scoped (2 Stories, backend vs FE)
decisions.detail: Both Stories already follow the {役割}として、{やりたいこと}をしたい。なぜなら、{理由}だから。 format — no rewrite needed. Granularity: despite the investigation surfacing a much larger real file-touch surface than the ROADMAP's 2-Task-per-Story hint implied (see the 'scope discovery' decision below), everything discovered is interdependent plumbing for exactly ONE user-facing behavior per Story ('codex/opencode become usable via config+registry+notify on the backend' / 'a user can create and use a codex/opencode tab from the GUI with working capability badges'). None of the sub-pieces (config.toml surface, GET /api/agents, hook.go --agent dispatch, shared_profile bind-mount, notify-hub agentKind stamping) are independently shippable/valuable on their own — per story-scenarios.md granularity guidance this stays ONE Story, not a split. Tasks were expanded within each Story instead (see ROADMAP mutations) to make the real scope legible to the Run-phase implementer.

decisions.title: Scope discovery: the ROADMAP's Task list undersold the actual gap — this is a graft from the `maultiagent` reference branch, not new-from-scratch work
decisions.detail:
ROADMAP's S2b5691-1 Task list only said 'main.go にcodex/opencode registry登録を追加' + 'in-container実行の実機検証', implying a ~1-line main.go change. Actual investigation (reading internal/agent/registry.go, cmd/palmux/main.go's agent.BuildRegistry call site, grepping for /api/agents and --agent=) found FIVE distinct, currently-unimplemented pieces: (1) internal/config has NO [agents.*] TOML surface (MasterConfig has no Agents field) so BuildRegistry is unconditionally called with a nil agents map — codex/opencode can never be registered no matter what main.go does without this; (2) GET /api/agents does not exist anywhere in internal/server; (3) cmd/palmux/hook.go parses --agent= into nothing (parseHookArgs only recognizes --event/--url) — a codex or opencode notify firing today either posts nothing (codex passes its JSON as the LAST argv element, which the current stdin-only reader never sees) or posts garbage (opencode's stdin JSON has a completely different schema than Claude's hook_event_name-based one, and would silently fail buildHookBody's switch); (4) internal/runtime/incus/shared_profile.go has no SetAgentSharedPaths method, so even a successfully-registered codex/opencode adapter's ContainerBinary/SharedContainerPaths would never reach a workspace container's bind-mounts; (5) the FE has no agent-picker/agent-tui-renderer/notify-capability-badge machinery at all (tab-bar.tsx hardcodes 'new-bash'/'new-claude' commands only, claude-tui-tab.tsx's WS URL builder has no kind segment matching agenttab.Provider's actual route shape).

Crucially, ALL FIVE pieces already exist, fully implemented and REAL-INCUS LIVE-VERIFIED (real codex-cli 0.144.1, real opencode 1.17.18, real incus container — docs/sprint-logs/S339021 on the `maultiagent` branch, git branch still present locally: `git branch -a` shows `maultiagent`), because this codebase's own history (CLAUDE.md's S0e8afb entry, and the 'maultiagent multi-agent branch' memory note) describes S0e8afb as HAVING DELIBERATELY GRAFTED ONLY internal/agent/** verbatim and explicitly deferred registry registration + FE exposure to 'a future Story' — which is this Sprint. maultiagent predates the S3f2658/S862203 no-halt-agent ptyhost work that has since landed on main, so none of its diffs apply as a clean cherry-pick/merge; each file must be manually re-applied onto main's current (post-ptyhost, post-S1f75ec, post-Sadf90e) structure — the exact same process S0e8afb already used successfully for internal/agent/** and the agenttui daemon/manager graft (see docs/sprint-logs/S0e8afb/verification-S0e8afb-2.md for that precedent's own description of the technique). This changes the Run-phase implementer's job from 'implement a new feature' to 'port + adapt a known-working, previously-live-verified reference implementation', which meaningfully de-risks the Sprint versus the ROADMAP's original framing — see the returned implementation_notes for the exact maultiagent commit hashes / `git diff main maultiagent -- <path>` invocations to use as reference per file.
decisions.reference: internal/agent/registry.go, cmd/palmux/main.go:605-680, cmd/palmux/hook.go, internal/runtime/incus/shared_profile.go, frontend/src/lib/tab-registry.ts, frontend/src/components/command-palette/command-palette.tsx; maultiagent branch commits b42aab6 (Sdec0a7-2), e7ae79c/b56c2d1 (Sdec0a7-3), ef3da64/cab59a7 (S339021-3), 1ff1994 (in-container)

decisions.title: codex/opencode registration is config-gated, not auto-enabled by binary presence
decisions.detail: Considered two designs: (A) main.go unconditionally passes codex/opencode entries to agent.BuildRegistry whenever the binaries resolve on PATH (auto-detect), vs (B) port the maultiagent reference's [agents.*] config.toml surface verbatim, where codex/opencode only register when the operator explicitly writes an enabled [agents.codex]/[agents.opencode] section (D3 in maultiagent's own S339021 decisions.json: 'codex/opencode become BUILT-IN adapters in agent.Registry (like claude), superseding the generic [agents.codex/opencode] path... but the dedicated adapter logic is used' — i.e. the config section still gates whether they appear, only the DISPATCH target differs from a plain GenericAdapter). Chose (B): matches DESIGN_PRINCIPLES priority 7 (明示的>暗黙的 — no silent host-fingerprinting magic), avoids a real UX regression where every host with codex/opencode installed for unrelated reasons would suddenly grow 2 new always-on TabBar groups (agenttab.Provider seeds Min=1 unconditionally once registered — there is no 'registered but hidden' state in the current tab.Provider model), and reuses a real, already-tested reference implementation rather than inventing a new gating mechanism. Consequence: AC-S2b5691-1-1/1-2's wording ('registry にcodex/opencodeアダプタが登録されている' / 'GET /api/agents がcodex/opencodeを含む一覧を返す') is clarified via ROADMAP jq mutation to state this is observed WHEN [agents.codex]/[agents.opencode] are enabled in config.toml, not unconditionally on every host — this is a wording clarification of already-true intent (the Sprint title itself says 'registry登録', not 'デフォルト有効化'), not a scope cut.
decisions.reference: maultiagent docs/sprint-logs/S339021/decisions.json D3-builtin-not-generic; DESIGN_PRINCIPLES.json priority_rules[9] (明示的>暗黙的)

decisions.title: Story scenario derivation — Story 1 classified 'mixed', Story 2 classified 'gui'
decisions.detail: Story 1's user is an operator editing config.toml (cli-adjacent) plus any API client reading GET /api/agents plus a real-incus-container observation for AC-1-3 — none of these alone is Story 1's sole entry point, so 'mixed' per story-scenarios.md. Story 2 is unambiguously 'gui' (tab-add picker, ⌘K palette, Activity Inbox badge) per the project-level default-on rule (this project has a React frontend and every AC is browser-observable) — ran the GUI spec process in autonomous mode, wrote docs/sprint-logs/S2b5691/gui-spec-S2b5691-2.json with a Mermaid state diagram, endpoint contracts (including the not-yet-existing GET /api/agents, marked registered:false so Story 1 landing is legible as a precondition), and data-testids.

decisions.title: AC-S2b5691-1-3 (real in-container exec) scenario derivation: attempted as a real, automatable scenario rather than an immediate MANUAL SMOKE handoff
decisions.detail: Per DESIGN_PRINCIPLES priority_rule 0/1 (never skip AC; reproduce the real failure-inducing condition, not toy data), checked whether this exact planning environment can execute the real scenario: `which codex opencode incus` all resolved (codex-cli 0.144.1, opencode 1.17.18, incus client+server 7.1) and `findmnt -no SOURCE /` shows a real LVM root, not an incus-container overlay path — i.e. this is the real host, not a nested palmux workspace container (per CLAUDE.md's own container-detection heuristic). This matches the exact codex/opencode versions the maultiagent reference branch was live-verified against. So scenario-S2b5691-1.json's scenario-4 (real-incus-in-container) is written as a for-real, automatable scenario to attempt during Run/Verify — with an explicit escalation_if_infeasible clause instructing the Run/Verify phase to fall back to a human MANUAL SMOKE flag (not a silent mock substitute) if this exact environment turns out to differ from what Plan observed. Also flagged: the Run/Verify phase MUST use a throwaway/isolated palmux2 instance + config-dir + incus instance for this (never the instance the current Claude session's own tmux/palmux2 is running under — see CLAUDE.md 'palmux2 自身の中で palmux2 を開発するときの注意' and the incus-admin group gotcha memory note).
decisions.reference: DESIGN_PRINCIPLES.json priority_rules[0], priority_rules[1]; CLAUDE.md palmuxOS/self-hosting section; project_incus_group_gotcha memory

decisions.title: Execution wave: sequential (Story 1 then Story 2), not parallel
decisions.detail: Story 2's FE work has a hard runtime dependency on Story 1's backend: agent-registry-store.ts calls the real GET /api/agents (which does not exist until Story 1 lands), the agent-tui renderer's WS URL must match agenttab.Provider's actual route (backend-defined), and AC-S2b5691-2-2's real E2E ('simple turn actually runs') requires the backend registry + hook dispatch + shared_profile wiring to be functionally correct end-to-end, not just present. A parallel worktree for Story 2 would either have to stub/mock GET /api/agents (violating the project's real-server E2E discipline for anything beyond the mock.spec.ts edge-case file) or sit idle waiting for Story 1 to merge. Sequential avoids both. This also matches how the maultiagent reference branch itself sequenced these (Sdec0a7-2 backend merged before Sdec0a7-3 FE branch was cut).
decisions.reference: story-scenarios.md API scenario rules; gui-spec.md Phase 4 (mock vs e2e split)
